result.topic_en: This two-page spread gives Theorems 9 and 10, tables showing whether a prime 2p+1 divides a^p+1 or a^p−1 for a = 12, 13, 14 and 15, according to the residue class of 2p+1 modulo 4a.

items.quote: Sumto $a = 12$, si fuerit $2p+1$ numerus primus, utrum per eum divisibilis sit sive forma $12^p + 1$, sive $12^p - 1$, ex sequenti tabella patet
items.english: Taking a = 12, if 2p+1 is a prime number, whether the form 12^p + 1 or the form 12^p − 1 is divisible by it is evident from the following table (by residue class of 2p+1 modulo 48).

items.quote: Sumto $a$ successive $= 13, 14, 15$, si fuerit $2p+1$ numerus primus, utrum per eum divisibilis sit sive forma $a^p + 1$, sive $a^p - 1$, ex sequentibus tabellis patet.
items.english: Taking a successively = 13, 14, 15, if 2p+1 is a prime number, whether the form a^p + 1 or the form a^p − 1 is divisible by it is evident from the following tables (by residue class of 2p+1 modulo 52, 56, 60 respectively).
